gap: No result ChatGPT got lists which Sonos speakers can take a Bluetooth turntable and share it to the rest of a Sonos system: Arc Ultra, Beam Ultra, Era 100, Era 100 SL, Era 300, Move 2, Roam, Roam 2, Roam SL and Sonos Play. The original Move is not on Sonos's list, and the speaker has to stay grouped and set up on WiFi.
standout_why: I compared against turntableverse.com (rank 1–2 in both chats), the What Hi-Fi? Bluetooth turntables page (cited), the Louder best record players page (cited) and Turntable Lab (the retailer ChatGPT showed). Turntableverse covers codecs (SBC/aptX/aptX Adaptive for the AT-LP70XBT and PS-LX3BT), the AT-LP70XBT's AT-VMN95C / VM95-series stylus and general Sonos advice. On Sonos it only says 'Sonos says its Bluetooth-capable speakers can pair with a Bluetooth turntable' and does not list which Sonos models can, or the grouping and surround exclusions. The What Hi-Fi? and Louder pages came back with only their titles, so I could not check their full text and cannot rule out that they cover this. ChatGPT itself offered 'Sonos or other wireless home audio system' as a follow-up but never answered it.
decides: Confirms the pick rather than changing it. Any of the three Bluetooth decks (AT-LP70XBT, AT-LP60XBT, Sony PS-LX3BT) can feed a Sonos system, but only if the receiving speaker is on Sonos's Bluetooth-share list and is not set up as a surround. For a Sonos owner the speaker they own decides whether Bluetooth works at all. On the turntable side, the AT-LP70XBT ($299) takes any VM95-series stylus, while the AT-LP60XBT ($259–279) is limited to the ATN3600L and has a 3.5 mm line out instead of RCA. That supports ChatGPT's LP70XBT 'upgrade potential' claim with part numbers.

findings.label: Sonos Bluetooth-share requirements

findings.label: Sonos exclusion: speakers used as surrounds
findings.value: 'Bluetooth functionality is disabled' while supported speakers are set up as surrounds
findings.source_title: Share Bluetooth audio with your Sonos system (Sonos support)
findings.note: So an Era 100 used as a surround behind an Arc/Beam cannot receive a Bluetooth turntable.

findings.note: Swap is different from grouping. Roam can still group and share.
